title: Planck spectra: the Sun peaks near 500 nm
caption: Planck's law at 5000, 5800 and 6500 K (intensity per unit wavelength, relative). Wien's law λ_maxT = 2.898 × 10⁻³ m K puts the peak at 500 nm for 5800 K, matching the Sun's observed 500 nm, so T ≈ 2.898 × 10⁻³/(5 × 10⁻⁷) = 5796 K. Hotter bodies are brighter at every wavelength and peak at shorter ones.
alt: Three Planck curves against wavelength with peaks near 446, 500 and 580 nm; the hotter curve is higher and peaks further left.
description: The horizontal axis is wavelength in nm, the vertical axis relative spectral intensity.
Each curve is ∝ λ⁻⁵/(e^{hc/λk_BT} − 1). Peaks: 6500 K at 446 nm, 5800 K at 500 nm, 5000 K at 580 nm (Wien's law).
A peak at 500 nm gives T = 5796 K, the Sun's surface temperature, about 5800 K.
The curve of the hotter body lies above the cooler one at every wavelength.
